questions.q: Where in the lifecycle does this lesson say an ARB operates, relative to change control and the CAB?
options: After production deployment, as a final audit
At exactly the same point in time as the CAB, as an alternative to it
At design time, before significant build work begins -- earlier than change control, the CAB, or the go/no-go checkpoint
Only after an incident has already occurred
questions.explain: The ARB operates at design time, before anything concrete exists to evaluate for deployment safety -- earlier than every other review mechanism covered in this course.

questions.q: Per this lesson, how does the data dictionary (from Lessons 13-14) help an ARB in practice?
options: It lets the ARB check a proposal against documented existing structure in minutes, instead of relying on institutional memory to catch duplication
It has no relevance to ARB review
It automatically rejects any proposal that touches a documented field
It replaces the need for an ARB meeting entirely
questions.explain: A maintained data dictionary lets an ARB quickly check whether a proposal duplicates existing structure, rather than depending on someone simply remembering what already exists.

questions.q: Why does this lesson warn against having an ARB review every single proposed field or report?
options: Because ARBs are not allowed to review declarative changes under any circumstances
Because reviewing everything would create an even worse bottleneck than an overloaded CAB, since the ARB sits earlier in the lifecycle and would slow far more work for far less benefit
Because fields and reports can never contain architectural risk
Because only Apex changes are eligible for ARB review
questions.explain: The lesson applies the same risk-tiering logic from Lessons 1, 4, and 5 one step earlier: significance-based triggers keep the ARB focused on proposals that actually warrant design-time review.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe the relationship between an internal ARB and Salesforce's own CTA review process?
options: They are the exact same process under two different names
An ARB can only be run by Salesforce-certified CTAs
The CTA process replaces the need for any internal ARB

An internal ARB is not the same thing as the CTA certification process, but borrows the same underlying discipline of evaluating a design against real trade-offs and alternatives before committing to build it
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that an internal ARB isn't an industry certification process, but shares the same discipline of rigorous, alternatives-based evaluation that the CTA review culture is known for.

questions.q: Which of the following would this lesson's checklist flag as a reason for ARB concern?
options: A proposal that follows an already-established field-naming pattern with no new dependencies
A new custom object proposed to track data that an existing, lightly-used custom object already captures under a different name
A routine report built entirely from existing, already-reviewed fields
A picklist value addition following the org's existing conventions
questions.explain: Duplicating existing structure -- the exact Worked Scenario 2 failure from Lesson 12 -- is the first concrete check this lesson's ARB checklist names.
